newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLO TRADERS EYE U.S. DOLLAR, DATA, T-BOND CHARTS.
newsitem.headline: OLO TRADERS EYE U.S. DOLLAR, DATA, T-BOND CHARTS.

text.p: Belgian linear bond traders, usualy content with tracing the ups and downs of German bonds, kept a sharp eye on U.S. developments, as the OLO market remained virtually entirely focussed on the dollar/mark rate and its impact on European bonds.

The Bundesbank decision to leave rates unchanged Tuesday morning put all the more focus on U.S. developments, with U.S. July retail sales and producer prices, due at 1230 GMT on Wednesday, seen setting the direction of trade. Sales are seen up 0.7 percent, from 0.5 percent. The PPI is seen rising 0.1 percent, after falling 0.1 percent in June.
One chartist warned the U.S. T-bond futures chart was leaning on the support line of its April-July uptrend and had broken below that line intraday on August 8 and 11.
A close below the 112*10 level would be a break of the uptrend and a bearish signal, he said. The support line has been touched four times in the four-month rally.

The large allocation of funds at the weekly T-bill auction -- 150 billion francs, while only 126 billion was at maturity -- had little impact on money rates. Three-month paper closed at 3.52/54 percent from 3.50/54 Monday and 3.53 at the auction.
The frank closed at 20.6490/10 to the mark, 15 cents weaker.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
